records.quote: Prove that m (∠ ACB) = 1/2 m (∠ AMB).
records.text: R.T.P.: Prove that $m(\angle ACB) = \frac{1}{2} m(\angle AMB)$.

records.quote: There are three cases to prove this theorem.
records.text: Proof: There are three cases to prove this theorem.

records.quote: If M belongs to one of the two sides of the inscribed angle.
records.caption: Case 1: circle with centre M on side CA... M lies on chord CB; points C (top), A (right), B (bottom); segments CA, MA, with C, M, B collinear.

records.quote: If M is a point inside the inscribed angle.

records.quote: If M is a point outside the inscribed angle.
records.caption: Case 3: circle with M outside the inscribed angle; points C (top right), A (right), B (bottom), M (left of angle); dashed line through C, M extended; segments MA, MB, CA, CB.

records.quote: First case: If M belongs to one of the two sides
records.text: First case: If M belongs to one of the two sides of the inscribed angle.

records.quote: ∠AMB is outside Δ AMC
records.text: Since $\angle AMB$ is outside $\Delta AMC$; therefore $m(\angle AMB) = m(\angle A) + m(\angle C)$ (1). Since $AM = CM$ (radii lengths), therefore $m(\angle A) = m(\angle C)$ (2). From (1) and (2) we get: $m(\angle AMB = 2\, m(\angle C)$; therefore $m(\angle ACB) = \frac{1}{2} m(\angle AMB)$ (Q.E.D)

records.stem: A is a point outside the circle M, $\overrightarrow{AB}$ is a tangent to the circle at B, $\overrightarrow{AM}$ intersects the circle M at C and D respectively, $m(\angle A)=40^\circ$. Find with proof $m(\angle BDC)$.

records.label: Example
records.quote: Well known problem (1)
records.stem: Well known problem (1): If two chords intersect at a point inside a circle, then the measure of the included angle equals half of the sum of the measure of the two opposite arcs.
solution: R.T.P.: m(∠AEC) = ½ [m(arc AC) + m(arc BD)]
∵ m(∠AEC) = m(∠D) + m(∠A) = ½ m(arc AC) + ½ m(arc BD)
records.notes: Given line printed with overbars on AB and CD (chords) rather than segments.

records.label: Example
records.quote: Well known problem (2)
records.stem: Well known problem (2): If two rays carrying two chords in a circle are intersecting outside it, then the measure of their intersecting angle equals half of the measure of the major arc subtracted from it half of the measure of the minor arc in which both are included by the two sides of this angle.
solution: Proof: ∵ $\angle ABC$ is exterior to $\triangle BEC$.
records.notes: Solution has no separate final answer; ends with Q.E.D.

objectives.label: Identify
objectives.description: Identify an inscribed angle and the central angle subtended by the same arc in a circle.

objectives.label: Prove
objectives.description: Establish and prove that an inscribed angle is half the central angle subtended by the same arc.

objectives.label: Find
objectives.description: Find unknown angle measures in a circle using the inscribed/central angle theorem.

objectives.label: Use corollaries
objectives.description: Use the corollaries: an inscribed angle is half its arc, and an angle in a semicircle is a right angle.

objectives.label: Find angles formed by chords and secants
objectives.description: Find the angle between two chords intersecting inside a circle or two secants meeting outside it from the arcs they cut off.
